newsitem.title: USA: Texas Utils sees Comanche restart Thursday.
newsitem.headline: Texas Utils sees Comanche restart Thursday.

text.p: Texas Utilities Co said Thursday it plans to restart its 1,150 megawatt (MW) Comanche Peak 2 nuclear power plant some time later today.
The unit was knocked off line Wednesday by a lightning strike.
"They expect to bring it back later today," said company spokeswoman Pat Nichols, adding crews are trouble-shooting a control valve that was left valve partially open by the lightning strike.
The problem valve caused the main feed pump to fail, which in turn, tripped the unit out of service, she said.
Comanche Peak 2 could begin dispatch power to the regional grid later today, Nichols said.
"It usually takes 24 to 36 hours to return to full output," she said.
The adjoining Comanche Peak 1, which was unaffected by the Wednesday's lightning storm, was operating fully at its 1,150 MW capacity.
Texas Utilities had no trouble meeting its electricity demand due to unseasonably cool temperatures in the northern and central Texas regions, which are served by the utility.
"Our air-conditioning load is way, way down," she said.
The Comanche Peak units in Glen Rose, Texas, produce about 18 percent of the company's electricity deliveries.
